evidence.observation: "Milestone closure replays two source documents, a duplicate observation, one accepted group, one declined group and an interrupted restart. Compare the final model digest, surviving references, located evidence, decision identities, counters and terminal reason between uninterrupted and resumed runs."

The duplicate-observation growth is "The integrated test in tests/test_consolidation_loop.py", and the comparison is a separate "recovery comparison runs the same leave and merge in separate temporary workspaces". In the test file, test_recovery_matches_uninterrupted_history uses the workspace() fixture: two directly written facts with distinct codes 2 and 3, with no additive preview/apply and no duplicate tuple. test_located_additive_growth_then_consolidation has no interruption and no uninterrupted/resumed comparison. Its decline happens only inside `while set(info["group"]["members"]) != desired`, so it may leave zero groups.

concerns.recommendation: Add one replay test that does all of the following in one run: additive growth from a second document with a duplicate observation, a guaranteed leave, an accepted merge, and an interrupted restart. Compare the uninterrupted and resumed runs field by field. Alternatively, have the close ruling explicitly accept the split and explain why it is equivalent.
concerns.title: Amendment 5 closure replay is split into separate tests, and no single run contains all five required elements

evidence.observation: "Put the replay and exact results in the milestone close record."

The section only describes what the tests compare ("It compares the complete model bytes, all durable decision fields (including IDs and work counters), and the resulting report and terminal reason"). It records no final model digest, decision IDs, counter values, terminal reason string, pytest summary or test node IDs.

concerns.recommendation: Record the exact observed values from the replay: model sha256, decision IDs, items/pairs counters, the terminal reason (for example no-eligible-group) and the verbatim pytest summary for the named tests, each tied to the code commit that produced it.
concerns.title: The close record describes the replay but gives none of its exact results

evidence.observation: "The post-repair focused and RF6 checks returned 32 passed in 17.73s before the directory-alias regression was added. The phase structure, CLI, packaging, install, doctor, disclosure and CG1–3 selection on the earlier implementation returned 1053 passed... The wheel test preceded the final review repairs."

"Shared sample population evaluation now serves both additive admission and the reviewed mutation check." This changes the CG1 admission path, but the only check reported on the final bytes is "16 passed" for tests/test_consolidation_loop.py. The front-matter gate also lists `pytest -q tests/test_consolidation_loop.py tests/test_rf6_query_policy.py` with exit 0, while the prose says that run predates the final test.

concerns.recommendation: Re-run the CG1–3 selection, the packaging/install checks and the offline-wheel terminal example on the final commit. Record the verbatim summaries, and make the gate front matter match the prose.
concerns.title: Broad, CG1 and packaged-wheel checks were not re-run on the final code after the shared admission refactor

evidence.observation: "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold" and "Terminate when no eligible unresolved group meets the selected minimum score". src/gnd/evolve/consolidation.py filters on `g["score"] >= minimum_score` (default 0), but every step() call in tests/test_consolidation_loop.py uses the default. The only no-eligible-group result comes after all groups are resolved.

concerns.recommendation: Add a test that sets minimum_score just above and exactly at an eligible group's score. Assert no-eligible-group on one side and needs-decision on the other, and report the result in the close record.
concerns.title: The configured minimum-score stop is never tested on either side of the threshold

evidence.observation: "The replay simulates process interruption at publication and finalization boundaries." In the tests, the pre-finalize case (test_stale_unstaged_intent_can_be_superseded) replaces EvolutionService.apply entirely ("before staging"). It then appends to the model and asserts "superseded-before-publication", so nothing interrupted at publication is recovered to completion.
"It injects an interruption at finalization after the model CAS." Only the finalization interruption gets an equivalence comparison.

concerns.recommendation: Either narrow the claim to "before staging (supersession) and after CAS at finalization", or add an interruption between evidence staging and the model CAS whose recovery is compared with an uninterrupted run.
concerns.title: The publication-boundary interruption claim is broader than the tested before-staging case

evidence.observation: "Bound the loop by maximum decisions and discovery work." The only loop-bound tests are `step(path, max_items=0)` and `step(path, max_decisions=0)`. In consolidation.py, `spent` sums work only from state["completed"], so discovery work in read-only needs-decision calls is never charged, and max_pairs exhaustion is not tested at the loop level.

concerns.recommendation: Test the decision and items/pairs limits at exact and one-less values after at least one completed decision. Also state in the record whether probing steps count against discovery work.
concerns.title: Loop decision and discovery-work limits are tested only at zero, and probe work is not charged

evidence.observation: "Changing the supporting source of a declined group offers it again." test_changed_evidence_reopens_a_declined_group copies the other fact's existing span into fact 0's provenance.spans and rewrites model.orm.json directly. No new source document is supplied and no additive apply is used.

concerns.recommendation: Either describe the test as an evidence-span change, or reopen through a public additive apply that cites a new document.
concerns.title: The reopen-after-changed-evidence claim edits the model directly rather than changing a source through the public path

evidence.observation: "use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair" and "Milestone closure requires a replay across phases, a disposition for each issue and an inventory of unverified claims."

"The reporter's two large models were unavailable... No paid grower effectiveness trial was selected." The record does not say whether these were optional corpus trials or mandatory criteria. It also does not say whether the #338/#339 reproduction examples were run as acceptance pairs.

concerns.recommendation: Add a short table that marks each criterion mandatory or optional, links it to its evidence, and lists the unverified claims, including the reporter corpus counts.
concerns.title: The close record does not separate mandatory criteria from optional corpus trials or list the issue reproductions

response.summary: The CG3 workflow covers the four decisions, binds each decision to its digests and recovers after finalization, and the tests mostly match the descriptions. The milestone close does not yet meet Amendment 5. The required replay is split across tests that each lack part of what it must contain. The close record gives no exact replay results. The broad, packaging and CG1-adjacent checks ran on code older than the final bytes, even though the change refactored shared CG1 admission. The configured minimum-score stop is never tested.

evidence.observation: “Milestone closure replays two source documents, a duplicate observation, one accepted group, one declined group and an interrupted restart. Compare the final model digest, surviving references, located evidence, decision identities, counters and terminal reason between uninterrupted and resumed runs.”

“The integrated test” performs additive growth and a merge, while “The recovery comparison runs the same leave and merge in separate temporary workspaces.” In tests/test_consolidation_loop.py, test_located_additive_growth_then_consolidation does not interrupt or compare resumed outcomes; test_recovery_matches_uninterrupted_history starts with prepopulated facts and does not run additive preview and apply.

concerns.recommendation: Run one uninterrupted and one interrupted execution of the full two-document, duplicate-observation, leave-and-merge scenario, and record the required field-by-field comparison.
concerns.title: The required combined closure replay is unproven

evidence.observation: “Review one group at a time against source spans” and “A mutation uses one digest-bound proposal for the entire group.” In src/gnd/evolve/consolidation.py, _check_mutation rejects unrelated object removals but does not reject modifications to unrelated surviving objects. A proposal can merge the selected fact group and also rename an unrelated object type while satisfying that guard.

concerns.recommendation: Reject proposal changes outside the selected group and its necessary row or role rewrites; add a regression with a valid unrelated object modification in the same proposal.
concerns.title: A reviewed group can carry an unrelated model change

evidence.observation: The gates list successful focused checks, but the narrative says “The post-repair focused and RF6 checks returned 32 passed in 17.73s before the directory-alias regression was added.” It also says the 1053-test selection ran “on the earlier implementation” and the wheel test “preceded the final review repairs.” No result on the final CG3 bytes is recorded.

concerns.recommendation: Run the affected focused and packaging checks on the final CG3 bytes and record their commands and results before claiming the gates passed.
concerns.title: CG3 results precede the final repair and regression

response.summary: The close evidence does not demonstrate the required combined recovery replay or verification of the final CG3 bytes. The consolidation guard also permits changes outside the reviewed group.

evidence.location: frontmatter gates and evidence blocks; body paragraph beginning 'Focused result'
evidence.observation: Gates declare "pytest -q tests/test_consolidation_loop.py --tb=short" and "pytest -q tests/test_consolidation_loop.py tests/test_rf6_query_policy.py --tb=short" at "exit: 0", and evidence pins "path: tests/test_consolidation_loop.py" with "sha256: 8d6b728550efe0679efc7966008e9aaa9899c2cc468642659a4edea3ab3c3580". The body states: "Focused result: 16 passed in 10.13s. The post-repair focused and RF6 checks returned 32 passed in 17.73s before the directory-alias regression was added." Both verbatim summaries are therefore recorded as captured before the final test was added to the very file whose digest is pinned, so no receipt in the artifact corresponds to the pinned bytes.
"Run the first spec's focused selection and retain its verbatim pytest summary."

concerns.recommendation: Re-run both pytest gates against the pinned tests/test_consolidation_loop.py bytes (sha256 8d6b7285...) and replace the two stale counts with the verbatim summary lines from those runs, noting the digest they were produced against.
concerns.title: Recorded gate summaries predate the pinned test file, so gate exit 0 is unevidenced

evidence.observation: "It compares the complete model bytes, all durable decision fields (including IDs and work counters), and the resulting report and terminal reason." The artifact reports that a comparison happens but contains no model digest, no counter value, no decision identity, no surviving-reference listing and no terminal-reason string anywhere in its 2057 bytes.

"Compare the final model digest, surviving references, located evidence, decision identities, counters and terminal reason between uninterrupted and resumed runs. ... Put the replay and exact results in the milestone close record."

concerns.recommendation: Add the exact compared values for the uninterrupted and resumed runs (final model digest, work-counter and decision counts, decision IDs, terminal reason text, surviving reference set) to the closure evidence, or submit the milestone close record that carries them for review alongside this delta.
concerns.title: Closure evidence omits the exact replay results amendment 5 mandates

evidence.observation: "Changing the supporting source of a declined group offers it again." This is the only statement about declined groups; the artifact nowhere records that a declined group with unchanged evidence is not offered again after restart.
"CG3: accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log and verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes." and "test both sides of every refusal."

concerns.recommendation: Record the negative-side result explicitly: after restart from the decision log with unchanged evidence, the declined group is absent from the offered set (with the counter or terminal reason showing it was suppressed), paired with the existing re-offer result.
concerns.title: Only the permissive side of the declined-group restart criterion is reported

evidence.observation: "The reporter's two large models were unavailable." and "Local samples and source provenance establish the checks' scope." The artifact does not state which #338/#339 reproduction steps were executed against local fixtures, nor that any reproduction step was skipped.

"Issue requirements come from [#338]..., [#339]..., including their proposed changes and reproduction examples." and "For each later phase, use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair, pin the old behavior on unextended inputs and record the public entry point and result." Also: "Native backend claims require native execution."

concerns.recommendation: State per issue which reproduction steps were run and against what inputs, and record the owner ruling that treats the reporter's large-model corpus trial as optional rather than as the §9 acceptance pair; if any reproduction step was not run, list it as an unverified claim rather than a boundary.
concerns.title: Mandatory issue-reproduction acceptance pairs are not shown to have been executed

evidence.location: ## Independent review and refactoring; frontmatter evidence
evidence.observation: "One reviewer is one reviewer." The section cites a single review and ledger: "The [review](notes/reviews/CG3-r1/independent-review.md) found two group-scope issues..." and evidence pins only "tests/test_consolidation_loop.py" and ".gnd-planning/milestones/cross-document-growth/notes/reviews/CG3-r1/independent-review.md", while the body asserts "Delegated acceptance (auto=true) on November 28, 2026."
"Each phase needs its own spec and owner ruling, implementation, focused tests, independent diff review, refactoring review and numbered record."

concerns.recommendation: Either add the digest-bound refactoring review artifact for CG3 as a distinct seat, or record the owner's explicit waiver of the second seat in this station so the acceptance claim matches plan §8.
concerns.title: Plan §8 requires an independent diff review and a refactoring review; only one seat is evidenced

evidence.observation: "A pre-publication stale intent is superseded only before evidence staging." and "Divergence after staging requires reconciliation." No refusal, digest check or test is recorded for a proposal whose reviewed model digest no longer matches once staging has begun.

"Bind each decision to group and evidence hashes and the reviewed model digest." and "A mutation uses one digest-bound proposal for the entire group, including row moves and role rewrites." and "Check constraint conflicts and dangling references before applying."

concerns.recommendation: Record the digest-mismatch behavior after staging as an explicit refusal with a test result, or state that recovery completes the originally digest-bound proposal unchanged; do not leave the path to an undefined reconciliation step.
concerns.title: Stale-intent handling is bounded only 'before evidence staging', leaving post-staging divergence to unspecified reconciliation

evidence.observation: "The journal and model directory are locally trusted. The workflow needs POSIX directory locking for journal writers." The artifact records no implemented lock, no refusal when locking is unavailable, and no test for concurrent writers.

"Persist proposal and decision identity before publishing, and complete the existing transaction on recovery." and "Demonstrate failed rewrites leave both rows and references intact and restart after publication completes the ledger once."

concerns.recommendation: Either evidence the directory lock and a concurrent-writer or lock-unavailable refusal test, or record an owner ruling that single-writer operation is a documented precondition of the shipped skill so the residual is scoped rather than open.
concerns.title: Declared need for POSIX directory locking is an unmet precondition with no guard or ruling

evidence.observation: "A separately installed offline wheel ran the packaged terminal example and recorded one leave before reporting a different group. The wheel test preceded the final review repairs."
"CG3 owns the packaged consolidation skill and its installed example." and "Run existing examples and compare the observable result for a caller using the previous interface."

concerns.recommendation: Re-run the installed offline wheel example against the post-repair build and record its observable output next to the pre-repair result, so the packaged entry-point claim rests on shipped bytes.
concerns.title: Packaged terminal skill was only exercised on a wheel built before the final review repairs

evidence.observation: "The phase structure, CLI, packaging, install, doctor, disclosure and CG1–3 selection on the earlier implementation returned 1053 passed, 2 deselected in 170.41s." The artifact attributes the only broad regression number to "the earlier implementation" and offers no equivalent run against the final CG3 bytes.
"The product changed on the milestone branch."

concerns.recommendation: Either record a post-repair broad selection run with its verbatim summary, or label the 1053-passed figure as superseded so the closure ruling does not treat it as verification of the shipped code.
concerns.title: The only whole-suite count is explicitly attributed to a superseded implementation

evidence.observation: "...supplies bytes for a second document and appends an already-observed tuple from its distinct cited occurrence." and "A separate stale-input control, a deontic constraint conflict, and an incomplete transfer leave original model bytes intact." The artifact never records the refusal of a repeated identical tuple at an identical source occurrence, nor a separated differing-excerpt versus differing-document test.

"A repeated identical tuple and source occurrence adds no evidence and is refused as redundant. ... Test differing excerpts and differing documents separately." and "test both sides of every refusal."

concerns.recommendation: Add the redundant-occurrence refusal result and the two separated negative controls (differing excerpt, differing document) to the closure replay description, or point to the phase record that carries their verbatim results.
concerns.title: Closure replay evidences only the admitting side of the duplicate-observation rule

evidence.observation: "Issues #338 and #339 remain open pending merge into the default branch." This is the only mention of the two issues; the artifact maps no requirement of either issue to a phase result.
"Milestone closure requires a replay across phases, a disposition for each issue and an inventory of unverified claims."

concerns.recommendation: Add a short per-issue disposition (for #338 and #339 separately: which §4 exit criterion and which recorded result discharges it, and what remains unverified) so merge status is not the only statement about the issues.
concerns.title: Closure evidence states merge status but no disposition per issue as §9 requires

evidence.location: frontmatter evidence; ## Independent review and refactoring; Delegated acceptance paragraph
evidence.observation: Evidence pins only "tests/test_consolidation_loop.py" and ".gnd-planning/milestones/cross-document-growth/notes/reviews/CG3-r1/independent-review.md", yet the body relies on unpinned bytes: "The [ledger](notes/reviews/CG3-r1/FINDINGS.md) binds each disposition to a repair." and "The integrated two-document sample replay and the uninterrupted/interrupted equivalence test are described in [closure evidence](notes/close-delta.md)."
"Plan and close require the project's four-reviewer bar, recorded against the reviewed bytes."

concerns.recommendation: Add sha256 entries for notes/reviews/CG3-r1/FINDINGS.md and notes/close-delta.md to the station evidence block so the repair ledger and closure claims are bound to the bytes the record relies on.
concerns.title: FINDINGS.md ledger and close-delta.md are load-bearing but absent from the digest-bound evidence list

response.summary: The CG3 record and closure delta describe a coherent consolidation loop, an integrated two-document replay and an interruption/restart comparison, but the results as submitted do not yet demonstrate the mandatory criteria. The recorded pytest summaries are explicitly pre-dated relative to the pinned test bytes, the closure evidence narrates the uninterrupted/resumed comparison without reporting any of the compared values that plan amendment 5 requires, and only the admitting side of several both-sides refusals (declined-group suppression, redundant identical occurrence) is evidenced. Packaged-wheel and broad-suite results are attributed to pre-repair or earlier implementations, and post-staging divergence plus journal-writer locking remain declared residuals without a guard, test or owner ruling. No origin-loss or journal-recovery failure is asserted by the bytes; the defects are unsupported or stale demonstration claims rather than observed breakage.

evidence.observation: The record claims "It compares the complete model bytes, all durable decision fields (including IDs and work counters), and the resulting report and terminal reason." but omits the exact results, final model digest, and test output required by plan amendment 5: "Put the replay and exact results in the milestone close record."

concerns.recommendation: Include the exact results of the replay (e.g., test output, counters, model digests, terminal reason) in the milestone close record to substantiate the claims and meet the plan amendment 5 requirement.
concerns.title: Milestone close record omits required exact results

evidence.observation: The phase document records test executions ("16 passed in 10.13s... ran the packaged terminal example") but omits the requirement from Section 9 to "use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair, pin the old behavior on unextended inputs".

concerns.recommendation: Update the CG3 phase document to explicitly record the pinned old behavior on unextended inputs and link the issue reproduction with the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair.
concerns.title: Phase CG3 omits pinned old behavior on unextended inputs

response.summary: Milestone close record omits exact results and pinned old behavior for later phases, violating plan mandates.

evidence.observation: The binding completion clause states: "Milestone closure replays two source documents, a duplicate observation, one accepted group, one declined group and an interrupted restart." This is listed among the five amendments that "supersede shorthand in the phase table" (line 71).

The recorded replay covers "a valid unattended model, supplies bytes for a second document", "an already-observed tuple from its distinct cited occurrence", "one digest-bound proposal with a row move and a deletion", and an interruption "at finalization after the model CAS" with a completing invocation. No declined group appears in this replay; the only declined-group evidence is a separate control: "Changing the supporting source of a declined group offers it again." The uninterrupted-vs-resumed comparison is therefore never shown to include a declined group's decision identity, work counters or terminal reason.

concerns.recommendation: Either extend the closure replay to include declining one group before the interruption so the resumed/uninterrupted comparison covers it, or record an explicit disposition explaining why a separate control satisfies amendment 5's mandatory replay composition.
concerns.title: Declined group absent from the amendment-5 closure replay

evidence.observation: The record states: "The post-repair focused and RF6 checks returned 32 passed in 17.73s before the directory-alias regression was added... The phase structure, CLI, packaging, install, doctor, disclosure and CG1–3 selection on the earlier implementation returned 1053 passed, 2 deselected in 170.41s... The wheel test preceded the final review repairs." The broad 1053-test verification and the packaged-wheel run both predate the final review repairs, so the post-repair state rests on the 32-test focused run alone.

concerns.recommendation: Re-run the phase-structure selection (or full suite) on the final post-repair bytes and record the verbatim summary, so the shipped state is covered by more than the focused consolidation/RF6 tests.
concerns.title: Broad-suite result predates final CG3 repairs

evidence.observation: The clause requires: "Put the replay and exact results in the milestone close record."

The close record describes the comparisons qualitatively ("It compares the complete model bytes, all durable decision fields (including IDs and work counters), and the resulting report and terminal reason") but records no actual counter values, terminal reason string, or final model digest. The exact values exist only inside the referenced test file, not in the close record itself.

concerns.recommendation: Append the recorded terminal reason, decision IDs, work counters and final digest (or a pointer-plus-summary block) to the close record so the close artifact alone carries the exact results amendment 5 demands.
concerns.title: Close record describes but does not record exact replay results

response.summary: The CG3 record and close-delta honestly document a two-document replay with duplicate observation, accepted group, interrupted restart and equivalence comparison, plus scoped residuals (no corpus trials, reporter models unavailable). One mandatory element of plan amendment 5 is not demonstrated as specified: the declined group is exercised only as a separate control, not inside the closure replay whose uninterrupted-vs-resumed comparison is the completion criterion. Two lower-grade gaps concern verification freshness and recorded exact results.

evidence.observation: "Focused result: 16 passed in 10.13s. The post-repair focused and RF6 checks returned 32 passed in 17.73s before the directory-alias regression was added. The phase structure, CLI, packaging, install, doctor, disclosure and CG1–3 selection on the earlier implementation returned 1053 passed, 2 deselected in 170.41s. A separately installed offline wheel ran the packaged terminal example and recorded one leave before reporting a different group. The wheel test preceded the final review repairs." The front matter (lines 10-11) asserts gate 2 "pytest -q tests/test_consolidation_loop.py tests/test_rf6_query_policy.py --tb=short" exited 0, but the only recorded count for that command (32 passed) predates the directory-alias regression, and the full-suite and wheel results are explicitly from before the final repairs.

concerns.recommendation: Re-run the combined focused+RF6 gate, the full phase selection and the offline-wheel example on the final tree and record the post-repair exact results (or annotate each gate with which bytes it ran against), so the phase record and the close demonstrably verify the shipped implementation rather than the earlier one.
concerns.title: Only the 16-test focused result is tied to the final bytes; combined, full-suite and installed-wheel verification all predate the final review repairs

evidence.observation: "The integrated test in tests/test_consolidation_loop.py takes a valid unattended model, supplies bytes for a second document and appends an already-observed tuple from its distinct cited occurrence." and "It compares the complete model bytes, all durable decision fields (including IDs and work counters), and the resulting report and terminal reason." The document records no counts, digests, compared values or verbatim output for the replay or the equivalence comparison.
"Put the replay and exact results in the milestone close record."

concerns.recommendation: Carry the replay's verbatim results into the closure record or the milestone close it feeds: the test summary line, the uninterrupted-vs-resumed model digest or byte-equality outcome, the compared decision identities and counters, and the terminal reasons, so amendment 5's exact-results requirement is met by the close artifact itself rather than only by the passing gate.
concerns.title: Closure evidence describes the replay and equivalence comparison but records none of the exact results amendment 5 requires in the close record

evidence.observation: "For each later phase, use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair, pin the old behavior on unextended inputs and record the public entry point and result."

"The reporter's two large models were unavailable." The boundaries scope the checks to "Local samples and source provenance establish the checks' scope", but neither this document nor the phase record states whether the issues' own reproduction examples were executed or lists them among the scoped residuals.

concerns.recommendation: Record whether the reproduction examples from #338 and #339 (distinct from the unavailable large models) and the pinned old behavior on unextended inputs were exercised with their results, or add them explicitly to the scoped-residual inventory so the mandatory acceptance pair is distinguished from the optional corpus trials the boundaries already scope.
concerns.title: Plan section 9's issue-reproduction acceptance pair is neither evidenced nor scoped out in the closure artifacts

response.summary: All three artifacts digest-matched. The CG3 record and closure evidence describe a two-document replay with duplicate observation, digest-bound proposals, all four decision kinds, budget-bounded terminal reasons and publication/finalization interruption recovery that match amendments 4 and 5 in shape, and the record's cited evidence digests (tests/test_consolidation_loop.py, CG3-r1 independent review) match the working tree. However, the only exact results tied to the final bytes are the 16-test focused run: the combined focused+RF6 count, the 1053-test full selection covering CG1-CG3, and the installed-wheel check all explicitly predate the final review repairs, and the closure evidence itself carries no exact results as amendment 5 mandates, while the plan section 9 issue-reproduction acceptance pair is nowhere recorded as run or scoped out.

criteria: Assess whether the results and scoped residuals meet the five plan amendments and issues 338 and 339. Identify material unsupported claims, conflicting constraints, origin loss or journal recovery failures with reproducible evidence.
Distinguish mandatory completion criteria from optional corpus trials. Assess the reported replay, boundaries and verification of all three phases.
